verdict.reasoning: The printed page (index p.847, PDF p.869, top of right column) shows 14 separate lines: two indented sub-entries of Implementation (Reserved words 4, Standard extensions 4), the top-level entry Implementor-defined with five indented sub-entries (Intermediate data item 122 ... Record types 706), five top-level entries (IMPLEMENTS clause 178, 183 through Implicit transfer of control 387), and the top-level entry IN phrase. page-869.md line 60 holds all of them as one space-separated paragraph with a three-space indent, as quoted. No words or page numbers are missing, but the line breaks carry the index hierarchy: the transcription no longer shows which entries are sub-entries of Implementation or of Implementor-defined and which are top-level, and the indent makes IN phrase and the IMPLEMENTS/Implicit entries look like sub-entries. That loss is more than reflow. It is a defect in non-normative index content only, so severity structural is right.
